question.worked_solution:
The integral is defined over a type II region.

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}y{e}^{x}\,dx\,dy & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}y{e}^{x}\,dx]dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[y{e}^{x}]_{0}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(y{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}-y{e}^{0})\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}({y}^{2}-y)\,dy\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{2}({y}^{2}-y)\,dy & ={[\frac{1}{3}{y}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{1}^{2} \\  & =(\frac{8}{3}-2)-(\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
